text:
samir: quick update — slot-evict policy canary finished on prod pool A (12 nodes). results look solid, dropping p50 by ~14% for short-seq chat workloads and reducing token CPU by ~7%. :tada:

anita: love to see numbers. can you paste the perf snapshot or link?

samir: here are the high-levels from the dashboard: p50 38ms -> 33ms, p95 210ms -> 205ms, tokens/sec per GPU +6.8%, cost per 1k tokens -7.1% (est). link: https://internal.redwood/reports/slot-evict/2050001111-summary

jess: nice. is this the soft-evict-by-slot heuristic we discussed? any user-visible regressions?

samir: yep same heuristic — evict smaller KV slots first when memory pressure hits soft threshold. no regression on long-seq tests, actually p99 unchanged. ran 48h soak and smoke evals ok.

kevin: what about canary rollout plan? fully automatic or manual?

samir: started as canary -> 10% -> 30% -> 100% over 4 hours. no error spikes or OOMs. final step executed at 2050001145.

deploy-bot: canary: slot-evict-policy v3.2 deployed to pool-A-canary at 2050001120. health checks OK.

anita: were there any edge cases in the perf tests? i remember some woven prompts causing worse prefix cache hitratio before.

samir: good call — we saw a small dip in prefix dedup hitratio for synthetic woven prompts (drop ~3%), but end-to-end latency still improved because memory churn decreased. flagged in the release notes and added a follow-up perf test.

kevin: can we get a one-pager for release notes? ops wants the rollout window and the risk section.

jess: i'll draft the release snippet. includes config flag name and recommended safe thresholds.

ops-bot: alert: autoscaling events +2 for pool-A between 2050001130-2050001140 (expected).

samir: thanks everyone. next steps: jess will push release note, kevin will add rollback playbook entry, anita will schedule a 30-min postmortem with runtime+ml to capture learnings.

anita: ack, scheduling now for tomorrow 10am PT.

samir: TL;DR: slot-evict v3.2 = p50 down ~14% for short-seq, cost -~7%, no service regressions. rolling to prod complete. :rocket:
